clue.text: One complaining about brother being back as dock chief

indicators.note: about places the complainer around the brother, holding him inside

parts.note: a whinger is someone who moans or grumbles

indicators.note: being back says the word for brother is read in reverse

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian monk or friar, a religious brother

explanation.surface: A grumbler is unhappy that his brother has returned as the harbour boss.
explanation.walkthrough: FRA is the title of an Italian friar, a religious brother; 'being back' turns it round, and 'about' wraps the complainer around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharfinger is the owner or keeper of a wharf, the person in charge at the dock.

clue.text: Trim up baby's first cradle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for trim is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to mow is to cut or trim grass

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word baby's

explanation.surface: Someone tidies the baby's first cot before it arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb is figuratively the cradle where life first grows, a place of origin.

clue.text: Assistant thought article should be leader

indicators.note: should be leader tells us the article letter goes from the end of the word to the front

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A helper reckons a newspaper article ought to be the lead story.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, typically to someone senior.

clue.text: Some poems, one more than Rasoumovsky got?

definitions.meaning: a sequence of four long poems by T. S. Eliot
Count Razumovsky was the dedicatee of three string quartets by Beethoven, so one more makes a set of four

explanation.surface: A question about whether a set of poems outnumbers what a Russian count received.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's three Razumovsky Quartets (Op. 59) were written for the Russian ambassador Count Razumovsky; the clue's spelling is an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's major work is a group of four poems, each titled after a place.

clue.text: Courage finally failing a Roman emperor

indicators.note: finally failing says the last letter of the word for courage is dropped

parts.note: nerve means courage or boldness

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler whose bravery eventually deserted him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally failing' drops the last E from NERVE to leave NERV.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerva was a Roman emperor who reigned briefly from AD 96 to 98.

clue.text: Fungus that's rare, you may recollect

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a mushroom being unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' looks like memory, but read as re-collect it means gather the letters of THAT'S RARE afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthstar is a puffball-type mushroom whose outer layer splits into a star shape.

clue.text: In present condition, need animal to carry one

indicators.note: to carry places the numeral within the animal, which bears it inside

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something needs a beast of burden to transport it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold as is means sold in its current state, without improvements or guarantees.

clue.text: What should secure conviction, avoiding another hearing

definitions.meaning: solid evidence that would convict in court
insulated so that nothing outside can be heard

explanation.surface: Strong evidence secures a guilty verdict and spares everyone a retrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court hearing, but means hearing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, it is reliable evidence; as one, a room that keeps out noise.

clue.text: City's pleasant look, welcoming queen to unfinished district

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for is, so the definition reads City is

indicators.note: welcoming has the look take the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: a smile is a pleasant facial look

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter of the word for district is dropped

parts.note: an area is a district

explanation.surface: An urban scene: a friendly expression greets the Queen in a half-built neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Square Mile is the City of London, its financial district; 'unfinished' cuts the last letter from the district word before it joins the queen inside the look.
explanation.definitionFit: The Square Mile is the nickname of the City of London, its financial heart.

clue.text: Spiritualist's choice not to be grilled too much

definitions.text: not to be grilled too much

parts.note: a medium is a spiritualist who claims to contact the dead
rare can mean exceptionally fine, like choice

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant picks how she would like her steak cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked so it stays pink inside is lightly cooked, not grilled for long.

clue.text: Opera heard in two small rooms

indicators.note: heard says the doubled word is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: a loo is a lavatory, a small room, and two of them make a doubled word

explanation.surface: Music performed in a pair of tiny chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is an unfinished opera by Alban Berg.

clue.text: Singular condition of status symbol on gown

definitions.meaning: the state of being single, unmarried
the academic hood worn over a graduate's gown showing a first degree

explanation.surface: Wearing an academic hood over one's gown marks a particular standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like strange, but means single, unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is the unmarried state of a man; as two, the hood a graduate wears.

clue.text: To drink, run for players' table

parts.note: squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: Team members are told to drink up and run to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUASH is a sweet fruit drink in Britain; LADDER is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is a ranking table of club players who challenge those above them.

clue.text: Entering name, record man as poet

indicators.note: Entering puts the abbreviation for name inside the record

parts.note: a log is a written record
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone writes a name in a log and describes the man as a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha.

clue.text: After arsenic, a time in critical state

indicators.note: After says the rest follows the arsenic symbol

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

indicators.note: in places the a and time within the word for critical

parts.note: severe means serious, critical

explanation.surface: A patient poisoned with arsenic is in a critical condition for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition, but it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare or assert solemnly.

clue.text: Attack on way — stifling scream

indicators.note: stifling has the way smother the scream within it

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a scream is something hilarious, a laugh

explanation.surface: An assault in the street, a cry muffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack or assault.

clue.text: In gutter, I'd a strange feeling of obligation

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters have become odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lying in the gutter had an odd sense of indebtedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is thankfulness, the sense of owing someone for a kindness.

clue.text: He supplied temple builders: take 'em on, I say

indicators.note: I say marks speech, so the phrase is spoken to give the name

parts.note: to take them on as staff is to hire them, said casually as hire 'em

explanation.surface: An employer's advice to a man who furnished the Temple workers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, King Hiram of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen for Solomon's Temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiram, king of Tyre, provided materials and workmen for building Solomon's Temple.

clue.text: Enormous resistance getting into Beowulf, for one

indicators.note: getting into puts the resistance letter within the word for the people

parts.note: Beowulf was a Geat, from a people of southern Sweden
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Huge opposition faces the hero of the Old English epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero of the poem Beowulf belongs to the Geats.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means very large, enormous.

clue.text: One's caught on the first morning

definitions.text: One's caught on the first morning

parts.words: One's caught on the first morning
parts.note: someone tricked by a prank on the morning of the first of a certain month

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested at dawn on day one.
explanation.walkthrough: Pranks on 1 April traditionally stop at midday, so victims are caught in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of an April 1st prank is fooled on that morning.

clue.text: Nixon's campaign slogan, short and to the point as race leader

indicators.note: short drops the final letter of the slogan

parts.note: Elect Richard, a plausible slogan for Richard Nixon
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Nixon's campaign message, brief and pithy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts ELECT RICHARD to ELECTRICHAR; 'short and to the point' poses as one phrase meaning pithy.
explanation.definitionFit: In greyhound racing the mechanical lure that the dogs chase leads the field round the track.

clue.text: Confection available in lethal variation

indicators.note: available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sweet comes in a deadly version.
explanation.definitionFit: Halva is a sweet made from sesame paste or semolina, a confection.

clue.text: Fearful, fail to cross river

indicators.note: to cross has the word for fail straddle the river letter

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A frightened person cannot get over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful, causing fear.

clue.text: Through which to view French town?

definitions.meaning: a glass element one looks through
a mining town in northern France

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders about a French town to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is the glass one looks through, and Lens is also a town in France.

clue.text: Sort of year's circuit: June finally enters

indicators.note: enters puts that letter within the circuit

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of June

explanation.surface: A runner's annual lap, with June ending inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February.

clue.text: One with sharp blade using craft to check temperature inside piece of pork

indicators.note: to check means to hold back, so the craft word surrounds and restrains the rest

parts.note: guile is craft or cunning

indicators.note: inside places the temperature letter within the cut of meat

parts.note: a loin is a cut of pork

explanation.surface: A butcher with a sharp knife uses a thermometer to test a pork joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to check' means hold back, so the craft word encloses the pork cut, and 'inside' puts the temperature letter within that cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillotine is the beheading machine with a heavy angled blade.

clue.text: Edge — the wicket falls

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: falls suggests the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes another wicket going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge' is a verb here, meaning sharpen; 'falls' shuffles THE plus W, the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet a knife is to sharpen it, give it an edge.

clue.text: Without esteem, in any case

definitions.meaning: lacking regard, read as regard plus -less

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict given no matter what.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless means anyway; split, it literally means lacking respect.
